answer: Disputed identities go to a jury drawn by verifiable randomness from a long-standing pool, such as an onyx-sealed lottery beacon fixed after votes are committed. Because a sybil farmer cannot predict seats, flooding the pool with fresh dune-thin accounts buys few jurors; seniority weights each ticket, like a terrace built layer by layer. Jurors who vote against the final consensus lose a deposit, so corrupting a majority costs far more than it earns.
